inbox.subject: Harborline capacity model, final
inbox.body:
Alex,

The capacity model is done and in the shared folder. Short version: a full launch puts 1,600 households into setup in January. At the 120 household caseload ceiling, with the 48 care leads we have and the Boston recovery work still eating hours, care leads can set up 800 households by December 31 and keep the promise from January 1.

That is 50% of forecast. My recommendation is we launch the Harborline partnership with 50% of forecast, 800 households by January 1, and bring the rest on in February and March waves. I would rather say that to Diane now than miss the promise in week two. Happy to talk at 3:30pm.

Jordan

inbox.subject: Sign-off needed: reporting floor before term sheet
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Before Julian sends the Harborline term sheet I need your sign-off on the reporting floor. Proposal: floor 25 for Harborline reporting, meaning no report we send them shows any count smaller than 25 people, at any cut (team, office, region). Diane asked for team level usage on Tuesday and some of their teams are under 20 people, so without the floor we could effectively identify employees using care support.

This matches our standing policy for employer and residence reports. A one line yes is enough.

Nadia

inbox.subject: Term sheet timing
inbox.body:
Alex,

I am aiming to send the Harborline term sheet to Diane Coleridge at 5pm today. Two things gate it: Nadia's reporting floor sign-off and whether we put 800 households by January 1 in the launch schedule instead of 1,600. Economics hold at $6 per employee per month, so $2.9M new ARR at full rollout either way.

A phased start does push some of it into Q1, which matters against the $1.2M forecast gap to the $19M year end plan. We can cover it on the 3:30pm.

Julian

inbox.subject: Lunch today and debrief agenda
inbox.body:
Morning Alex,

We are set for lunch at 11am in the main room, food from the place on Summer Street. Agenda for the debrief on the outage impact: what the care leads saw overnight, which households got late handoffs, and what we told families. Final numbers: recurrence lasted 3.2 hours, backlog peaked at 164 handoffs, 58 still open at 5am, all cleared by 8:10am.

The team is glad you are coming in person.

Keisha, Boston Care Operations

inbox.subject: Calloway Freight deck v3
inbox.body:
Alex,

V3 of the deck is attached. Renata Voss (VP People) and Malik Osei (Benefits Director) will be in the room. They have about 6,200 employees, mostly across New England.

I cut the AI slide down to one number, 70% of tasks closed by agents with no care lead touch, and put the Standing Plan 91% up front. Let's do 1:15pm to run it once.

Tomás

inbox.subject: Re: Next steps
inbox.body:
Hi Alex,

Thanks again for Tuesday. Owen and I are aligned internally and are looking forward to the term sheet. Our benefits committee meets on the 19th so anything we have by Monday works.

Owen will be the day to day contact on reporting once we are live.

Best,
Diane Coleridge, Harborline Mutual

newsletters.title: Open enrollment wrap: caregiving support climbs the wish list
newsletters.body: Employers finishing open enrollment report caregiving benefits among the most requested additions for 2027. HR leaders say the main barrier is proof of use without exposing individual employees, with several brokers now asking vendors for minimum group sizes in utilization reports.

newsletters.title: Winter planning for older adults living independently
newsletters.body: Residences are starting winter readiness checks. This week: medication refill timing around the holidays, fall prevention as days get shorter, and how families coordinate when relatives travel.

newsletters.title: Saying less, sooner
newsletters.body: A short essay on telling customers about capacity limits early. Phased launches with clear dates tend to preserve trust better than full launches that slip.
